t: Sew a button back on with a proper thread shank
desc: Use doubled, knotted thread. Lay a toothpick across the button, sew 6-8 passes through each pair of holes, remove the toothpick, wrap the thread around the stitches under the button to form a shank, and knot at the back.
check: Button attached to a real garment
Button passes through its buttonhole without the fabric puckering
Button doesn't move when tugged firmly

t: Do a practice tyre change on your own car, safely
desc: Flat ground, handbrake on, hazards on, wheel chocked. Loosen nuts a little before jacking, lift at the jacking point shown in the manual, swap the wheel, lower, then tighten in a star pattern. Never put any body part under the car.
check: Spare fitted and the original wheel refitted in a safe place
Nuts fully tightened in a star pattern once the car was lowered
Jacking point, tools and spare located without looking them up

t: Food safety: the danger zone and safe cooking temperatures
desc: Learn the temperature danger zone, the 2-hour rule, and safe internal temperatures for poultry and minced meat. Check your fridge temperature and whether you own a food thermometer.
check: What is the temperature danger zone and how long can perishable food sit in it?
What internal temperature makes poultry safe?
What internal temperature makes minced (ground) beef or pork safe?
a: Roughly 5-60 C (40-140 F). Refrigerate perishables within 2 hours, or 1 hour if it is above about 32 C (90 F).
74 C (165 F) in the thickest part.

t: Master knife basics: claw grip plus dice, mince, julienne and chiffonade
desc: With a sharp chef's knife and the claw grip (fingertips tucked, knuckles guiding the blade), dice an onion, mince garlic, julienne a carrot and chiffonade basil or spinach.
check: Onion diced into even pieces of about 1 cm
Carrot cut into matchsticks of roughly equal size
Claw grip used throughout with no cuts to fingers

t: Pan-sear chicken thighs and make a pan sauce from the fond
desc: Pat thighs dry, season, sear skin-side down in a hot pan until crisp, then cook through to 74 C inside. Deglaze the browned bits with stock or wine, reduce, and swirl in a knob of butter.
check: Thermometer reads at least 74 C in the thickest part
Skin crisp and deep golden
Sauce reduced until it coats the back of a spoon

t: Cook a classic rolled French omelette
desc: Beat 3 eggs with a pinch of salt. Cook in butter over medium-low heat, stirring and shaking the pan until softly set, then roll it onto a plate as a smooth, pale omelette.
check: Omelette rolled onto the plate in one piece
Outside pale yellow with no brown spots
Inside soft but set, with no runny raw egg

t: First aid: helping an unresponsive adult, recovery position and CPR
desc: Learn the sequence: check for danger, check response, open the airway, check breathing, call emergency services, then recovery position or CPR. Practise the recovery position on a willing friend.
check: How do you check whether someone is breathing normally?
When should you put someone in the recovery position?
What do you do if an adult is unresponsive and not breathing normally?
a: Open the airway with head tilt-chin lift, then look, listen and feel for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
When they are unresponsive but breathing normally; keep checking breathing until help arrives.
Call emergency services (speaker on), send for an AED, start chest compressions: centre of chest, 5-6 cm deep, 100-120 per minute.

t: First aid for burns, bleeding cuts and nosebleeds
desc: Learn the mainstream first-aid response for three common home injuries, then check your kitchen and bathroom for what you'd actually use (clean cloths, dressings, cling film).
check: How should you treat a minor burn?
How do you stop a nosebleed?
How do you control a bleeding cut?
a: Cool under cool running water for 20 minutes, remove rings or watches nearby, cover loosely with cling film. No ice, butter or creams.
Sit and lean forward, pinch the soft part of the nose for 10-15 minutes, breathe through the mouth; get help if it lasts over 20-30 minutes.
Firm direct pressure with a clean pad; if blood soaks through, add more on top rather than removing it. Call for help if severe.

t: Build a real monthly budget from your last 2-3 months of transactions
desc: Export recent transactions, put each into a category, and compute monthly averages for needs, wants and savings or debt repayment. Compare with a 50/30/20 split and set limits for 3 categories.
check: Every transaction for at least 2 months categorised
Monthly averages calculated for needs, wants and savings
Written limits for 3 categories, including one specific cut

t: Diagnose and fix a running toilet
desc: Add a few drops of food colouring to the cistern and wait 20 minutes without flushing. Colour in the bowl means a leaking flapper or seal; water spilling into the overflow tube means lower the float or adjust the fill valve.
check: Dye test done and the cause identified
Flapper replaced or float adjusted to match the cause
No running water sound 30 minutes after a flush

t: Write a one-page CV with achievement-based bullets
desc: Write a one-page CV: contact line, short profile, experience in reverse order with 3-4 bullets each that start with a verb and show a result (numbers where possible), then skills and education. Tailor it to one real job ad.
check: Fits on one page in a readable font size
Every bullet starts with an action verb and at least half include a measurable result
Proofread aloud with zero typos and 5 keywords from the job ad included

t: Unclog a sink with a plunger and by cleaning the P-trap
desc: Remove the stopper and pull out hair. Block the overflow with a wet cloth and plunge 15-20 times. If still slow, put a bucket under the U-shaped P-trap, unscrew it, clean it out and refit it hand-tight.
check: A full basin drains freely without pooling
No drips from the trap after a minute of running water
No chemical drain cleaner used

t: Negotiation basics: BATNA, anchoring and trading concessions
desc: Learn three core ideas, then plan a real negotiation (salary, rent, a bill, a second-hand purchase): write your alternative, your target, your walk-away point and two open questions to ask.
check: What is a BATNA and why does it matter?
What is anchoring?
Why trade concessions instead of simply giving them?
a: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement: what you'll do if there's no deal. It sets your walk-away point and your confidence.
The first number on the table pulls the final result toward it, so an ambitious but justifiable first offer helps you.
Free concessions signal more room to give. 'If you can do X, I can do Y' keeps the exchange balanced.

t: Cook a 3-dish dinner and serve everything hot at the same time
desc: Pick a main, a side and a simple dessert. Write a timeline counting back from serving time, do all the chopping and measuring first, and serve the hot dishes together.
check: Written timeline with a start time for each task
All prep done before the first pan went on the heat
Hot dishes served within 5 minutes of each other

t: Iron a dress shirt in the standard order
desc: Set the heat from the care label. Iron the collar (underside first), cuffs, sleeves, the yoke across the shoulders, the back, then the two front panels, using steam or a damp cloth for stubborn creases.
check: Shirt ironed in under 15 minutes
No new creases pressed into sleeves or front
Hung on a hanger straight away with the top button done up

t: Deep-clean your kitchen top to bottom, dry to wet
desc: Clear counters, dust high surfaces, degrease the hob, steam-clean the microwave with a bowl of water and lemon, empty and wipe the fridge, then floor last. Never mix bleach with vinegar, ammonia or other cleaners.
check: Fridge emptied, expired food binned and shelves wiped
Hob and microwave free of grease
Floor mopped last and the bin emptied and washed

t: Patch nail holes and small dents in a wall, ready for paint
desc: Scrape away loose bits, press lightweight filler in with a putty knife, scrape flush, let it dry fully, sand smooth with fine sandpaper, then touch up with matching paint.
check: All chosen holes filled and flush with the wall
No ridge felt when running a fingertip over each patch
Touch-up paint invisible from about 1 metre away

t: Meal-prep 5 lunches on a budget
desc: Cook one grain, one protein, two roasted vegetables and one sauce, then portion into 5 boxes. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours, eat within 3-4 days, and freeze any portions for later in the week.
check: 5 portioned boxes in the fridge or freezer
Cost per portion calculated
Food refrigerated within 2 hours of cooking

t: Home safety: smoke alarms, carbon monoxide and gas leaks
desc: Learn what to do about the three most common home hazards, then test your smoke alarm and check whether you have a carbon monoxide alarm near any fuel-burning appliance.
check: What should you do if you smell gas at home?
How often should you test smoke alarms, and when should they be replaced?
What are signs of carbon monoxide poisoning and what do you do?
a: Don't use switches, flames or plugs; open windows, turn off the supply at the meter if safe, get out and call the gas emergency line from outside.
Test monthly with the button; replace the whole alarm about every 10 years (or as the manufacturer says).
Headache, dizziness, nausea, tiredness, often better away from home. Get into fresh air, turn off appliances if safe, call for help.

t: How interest works: compounding, the rule of 72 and minimum payments
desc: Learn how interest grows savings and debts, then use a calculator on one of your own cards, loans or savings accounts to see what the figures mean in money.
check: What does the rule of 72 tell you?
What is compounding, and why is AER/APY higher than the nominal rate?
Why is paying only the minimum on a credit card expensive?
a: Years to double is roughly 72 divided by the annual rate: at 6% about 12 years. It works for debt growing too.
Compounding is earning interest on earlier interest. AER/APY includes it, so it beats the nominal rate when interest is added more than once a year.
Much of each payment goes to interest, so the balance shrinks slowly and you pay far more in total over many years.
